metadata.name: Gallstones (cholelithiasis) and biliary colic
metadata.emergency_level: Biliary colic routine; acute cholecystitis, cholangitis and gallstone pancreatitis are emergencies
metadata.severity: Often asymptomatic; complications can be serious

overview.short_description: Stones in the gallbladder, often asymptomatic, but able to cause biliary colic (episodic RUQ pain after fatty meals) and complications such as cholecystitis, obstructive jaundice, cholangitis and pancreatitis.
overview.detailed_description: Gallstones are very common and frequently asymptomatic (found incidentally). Symptomatic disease ranges from biliary colic to acute complications. Diagnosis is by ultrasound; management of symptomatic stones is usually cholecystectomy. The key tasks are distinguishing uncomplicated biliary colic from complications (fever, jaundice, persistent pain) and recognising emergencies (cholangitis, pancreatitis).
overview.pathophysiology: Supersaturation of bile with cholesterol (or pigment) forms stones; a stone transiently obstructing the cystic duct causes biliary colic, sustained obstruction/inflammation causes cholecystitis, and stones passing into the common bile duct cause obstructive jaundice, cholangitis or gallstone pancreatitis.
overview.etiology: Cholesterol stones (most) - risk with the 'five Fs' (female, forty, fertile, fat, family history); pigment stones with haemolysis. Rapid weight loss, pregnancy and certain drugs contribute.
overview.natural_history: Most asymptomatic stones remain silent; once symptomatic, recurrence and complications are more likely.
overview.prognosis: Excellent for uncomplicated disease treated with cholecystectomy; complications increase risk.

prevalence.value: Very common; a significant minority of adults have gallstones, many asymptomatic.

incidence.value: Increases with age, female sex, obesity.

mortality.value: Low uncomplicated; significant with cholangitis/severe pancreatitis.

risk_factors.lifestyle: High-fat/low-fibre diet, rapid weight loss, sedentary.
risk_factors.alcohol: Not a strong risk for stones.
risk_factors.medications: Oestrogens, some others; rapid weight loss (including after bariatric surgery).

chief_complaints.complaint: Episodic right-upper-quadrant/epigastric pain after fatty meals
Pain radiating to the back/right shoulder tip

symptoms.symptom: RUQ/epigastric pain, colicky, lasting up to a few hours (biliary colic)
Radiation to back or right shoulder
Fever with persistent RUQ pain and tenderness (cholecystitis)
Jaundice, dark urine, pale stools (+/- fever/rigors = cholangitis)

negative_findings.finding: Pain settles within hours, afebrile, no jaundice, normal LFTs
negative_findings.why_important: Supports uncomplicated biliary colic rather than a complication

negative_findings.finding: No epigastric pain radiating to back with very high lipase

history_questions.question: Is the pain in the right upper abdomen, after fatty meals, and does it settle within a few hours?
Any fever, or persistent pain (not settling)?
Any jaundice, dark urine, pale stools, or rigors?
Severe epigastric pain radiating to the back (pancreatitis)?
Risk factors (female, weight, family history, pregnancy)?

physical_examination.expected_finding: RUQ tenderness; Murphy's sign positive in cholecystitis

vital_signs.temperature: Normal in colic; raised in cholecystitis/cholangitis

laboratory_tests.expected_result: Normal in simple colic; obstructive pattern (raised bilirubin/ALP) with CBD stones

imaging.expected_findings: Gallstones; wall thickening/pericholecystic fluid (cholecystitis); dilated ducts
Ductal stones; ERCP for stone removal

ecg.when_needed: If epigastric pain could be cardiac
ecg.findings: Used to help exclude cardiac cause.

other_diagnostic_tests.endoscopy: ERCP for common bile duct stones (therapeutic)

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: Gallstones on ultrasound with compatible symptoms (biliary colic). Complications defined clinically/biochemically/radiologically: acute cholecystitis (RUQ pain >6h, fever, Murphy's sign, imaging changes); choledocholithiasis (obstructive LFTs, dilated CBD); cholangitis (Charcot's triad: RUQ pain, fever/rigors, jaundice); gallstone pancreatitis (raised lipase).

differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is it burning epigastric pain related to acid rather than fatty-meal RUQ pain?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Persistent pain, fever, positive Murphy's sign
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is the pain persistent with fever?
Any yellowing, dark urine, and fever/rigors?
Does it radiate to the back, come with exertion, or go to the groin?

diagnostic_questions.question: Any jaundice, dark urine, pale stools, fever/rigors, or pain that will not settle?
Is the pain in the right upper abdomen after fatty meals and settling within hours?
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: Typical -> arrange ultrasound and consider cholecystectomy

next_best_question.question: Any complication features (fever/jaundice/persistent pain/back radiation), and has an ultrasound been done?
next_best_question.branching_logic: Uncomplicated -> ultrasound + elective cholecystectomy referral + analgesia/advice; complications -> urgent/emergency admission (cholecystitis/cholangitis/pancreatitis)

red_flags.finding: Charcot's triad (RUQ pain, fever/rigors, jaundice) - cholangitis
red_flags.immediate_action: Emergency - admit; IV antibiotics, resuscitation, urgent biliary drainage (ERCP)

red_flags.finding: Persistent RUQ pain with fever/positive Murphy's sign (cholecystitis)
Severe epigastric pain radiating to back with raised lipase (gallstone pancreatitis)

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Acute cholecystitis, cholangitis, obstructive jaundice, gallstone pancreatitis (emergency).
referral_criteria.routine_referral: Symptomatic gallstones for elective cholecystectomy; incidental stones only if symptomatic/high-risk.

initial_management.supportive_care: Analgesia for colic; explain the diagnosis and plan; dietary advice while awaiting surgery.
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): NSAID; Paracetamol; Antibiotic. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_CG188.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Reduce fatty-food triggers while awaiting surgery; weight management.
initial_management.follow_up: Refer symptomatic stones for cholecystectomy; safety-net for complication features.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: Analgesia (NSAID or opioid) for biliary colic; antiemetics as needed. Definitive treatment for symptomatic stones is laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Complications need admission: IV fluids/antibiotics for cholecystitis/cholangitis, ERCP for ductal stones, and management of pancreatitis.

patient_education.home_advice: Gallstones are common and often cause no problems. When they do, they typically cause bouts of pain in the upper-right tummy, often after fatty meals, that settle within a few hours. The usual treatment for troublesome stones is keyhole surgery to remove the gallbladder. Seek urgent help if the pain does not settle, you develop a fever, or you notice yellow eyes/skin, dark urine or pale stools - these can mean a blockage or infection.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: حصوات المرارة شائعة وكثيراً ما لا تسبّب مشاكل. وعندما تسبّبها، تكون نوبات ألم في أعلى يمين البطن، غالباً بعد الوجبات الدسمة، تهدأ خلال ساعات. والعلاج المعتاد للحصوات المُزعجة هو جراحة بالمنظار لاستئصال المرارة. اطلب المساعدة العاجلة إذا لم يهدأ الألم، أو ظهرت حرارة، أو لاحظت اصفرار العين/الجلد أو بولاً غامقاً أو برازاً فاتحاً - فقد تعني انسداداً أو عدوى.
patient_education.prevention: Healthy weight, balanced diet, avoid very rapid weight loss.
patient_education.warning_signs: Persistent pain, fever, jaundice (yellow eyes/skin), dark urine, pale stools, or severe pain radiating to the back.

prevention.lifestyle: Healthy weight and diet; avoid crash diets.

evidence.evidence_level: High for cholecystectomy in symptomatic disease; established emergency pathways for complications.
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by NICE_CG188; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.

treatment_guidance.treatment_goal: Control biliary pain and provide definitive surgical/endoscopic care for symptomatic or complicated stones.
treatment_guidance.legacy_narrative_summary: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): NSAID; Paracetamol; Antibiotic. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_CG188.
required_history_before_any_medication: age and weight where dosing is weight- or age-dependent
pregnancy or breastfeeding status when relevant
documented drug allergies and the exact reaction
all prescribed, OTC, herbal and recreational substances
major cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal and bleeding history
non_drug_measures: No treatment is required for many incidentally found asymptomatic stones; avoid extreme rapid weight loss.

monitoring: renal function, blood pressure, oedema and gastrointestinal bleeding symptoms when clinically indicated
